title: SEC-4 (seeded): create credential files private from the start
head: 8fa491efedb19a4bb0da7aa97ab1363b4db74021
brief: Discord connect and Google connect created the token file with write_text at the umask mode and chmodded it afterwards; spotify_auth._store wrote a fixed <name>.tmp at umask mode and followed a symlink planted at that name. New jarvis/private_write.py write_private(path, data: bytes): unique temp name beside the target, created O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC at 0600, fsync, os.replace, temp unlinked on any failure. browser/host._write_private delegates to it; subagents._compact and stt_settings.update call it; the Spotify rotated token is still persisted before use. Tests: tests/private_writes_check.py checks per-writer modes (never wider than 0600), create flags, symlink refusal and rollback.
focus: correctness, including under concurrency and across the ordering of events
handling of untrusted input, and safety-boundary changes
test coverage of the new behaviour: would the tests fail without the change?
claims in the description against the evidence in the diff and tests

seeded.description: write_private creates the temp file wide (0o666) and narrows it with chmod after writing
seeded.patch:
diff --git a/jarvis/private_write.py b/jarvis/private_write.py
index 41f0af4..116be8a 100644
--- a/jarvis/private_write.py
+++ b/jarvis/private_write.py
@@ -33,12 +33,13 @@ def write_private(path: Path | str, data: bytes) -> None:
     """`data` to `path`, atomically, 0600, never through a symlink."""
     path = Path(path)
     tmp = path.with_name(f".{path.name}.{secrets.token_hex(4)}.tmp")
-    fd = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_CLOEXEC, 0o600)
+    fd = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_CLOEXEC, 0o666)
     try:
         with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
             handle.write(data)
             handle.flush()
             os.fsync(handle.fileno())
+        os.chmod(tmp, 0o600)
         os.replace(tmp, path)
     except BaseException:
         try:

ground_truth.mechanism: the temporary file is created at 0o666 (so 0644 under the usual umask) and only chmodded to 0600 after the data has been written and fsynced, so credential bytes sit in a group/world-readable file for a window; this is the exact bug the helper exists to remove, and it contradicts the module docstring ('never wider than 0600 for an instant')
ground_truth.location: jarvis/private_write.py write_private (os.open mode argument and the added os.chmod before os.replace)
ground_truth.evidence: with umask 022, stat the temp file between fsync and os.chmod: mode is 0644 while it holds the token; a check that only inspects the mode at os.replace time still passes
